name: AI Voice Agent SaaS + White-Label Platform (Flippa 12206758)
demand: The potential reseller audience is large but not the same as qualified buyers: Promethean Research’s 2026 industry report counts over 200,000 digital agencies worldwide and over 71,000 in North America; it does not estimate how many resell voice AI (https://prometheanresearch.com/digital-agency-industry-report/). In a RingCentral/G2 survey published 1 Oct 2026, 57% of surveyed leaders had voice AI deployed and another 10% were piloting it; 82% of live-deployment respondents who rated ROI reported positive ROI. This is a survey signal, not a population estimate or proof of this listing’s demand (https://www.ringcentral.com/us/en/blog/agentic-voice-ai-statistics/). The listing claims 1,000+ users in 40+ countries but separately shows 265 active subscribers; definitions and underlying records are not public (https://flippa.com/12206758-ai-voice-agent-saas-white-label-platform-1-000-users-40-countries-1-hr-day-owner-time-bootstrapped-recurring-revenue).
prices: The Flippa page advertises the target at $29/month plus $0.34/minute, with white-label plans from $297/month plus a transaction fee; terms and current customer price mix are not disclosed (https://flippa.com/12206758-ai-voice-agent-saas-white-label-platform-1-000-users-40-countries-1-hr-day-owner-time-bootstrapped-recurring-revenue). Current competitor pages show HelloAnswer at $99/month (https://www.helloanswer.ai/) and Call Supplai at $197/month (https://www.callsupplai.com/). These public prices indicate direct price competition; provider usage charges may be separate.

revenue_proof.claim: Flippa labels the listing Vetted + Data Verified and says its vetting team reviewed revenue, primary expenses, and traffic; Google Analytics and Stripe integrations are shown as connected. The public page hides the supporting records, and Flippa’s buyer guidance says financials are seller-provided inputs and recommends buyers obtain underlying evidence. Treat this as platform-reviewed seller data, not independently audited or buyer-verified revenue.
revenue_proof.claim_event_date: unverified; no underlying financial period or verification date is disclosed on the public page

revenue_proof.claim: The reopened public listing displays $7,282 monthly profit, 70% margin, $4,297 MRR, 265 active subscribers, 9% overall churn, and a $525,000 asking price. The supplied $350,000/$10.4K view conflicts with this public view. The current displayed price and profit imply about 6.0x annualized listed profit, matching Flippa’s displayed multiple, but the profit itself remains unverified to a buyer. MRR is also inconsistent with the stated profit and margin unless additional usage or other revenue is excluded from MRR; the listing provides no reconciliation.
revenue_proof.claim_event_date: unverified; the public page does not state the measurement month or churn period

copy_speed: Fast. New or newly announced adjacent offerings since Apr 2026 include ConnexŪS ATHENA (28 May; voice, email, chat) (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/05/28/3302893/0/en/Visium-Technologies-Subsidiary-Connex%C5%AAS-Ai-Launches-ATHENA-a-Compliance-Ready-AI-Agent-Platform-for-Voice-Email-and-Chat.html), Five9 Voice AI Agents (23 Jun) (https://five9.gcs-web.com/news-releases/news-release-details/five9-launches-breakthrough-new-release-voice-ai-agents-power), Helo Convo (7 Jul) (https://helo.ai/resources/newsroom/heloai-launches-helo-convo), OpenAI Presence for managed enterprise voice and chat deployments (22 Jul; adjacent, limited availability, not self-serve) (https://openai.com/index/introducing-openai-presence/), SkipHold Conversations, a white-label omnichannel layer (24 Aug) (https://skiphold.com/blog/conversations-launch-press-release), SkySwitch’s white-label AI Agent (1 Sep) (https://www.bcmone.com/company/press-releases/skyswitch-launches-native-ai-agent-bringing-enterprise-ai-communications-to-every-white-label-partner/), and Gupshup’s self-serve Voice AI platform (3 Sep) (https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/gupshup-launches-self-serve-voice-ai-platform-extending-conversational-engagement-into-phone-calls-302869131.html). These launches show rapid entry by both direct reseller platforms and larger adjacent vendors.
platform_risk: The listing names React, Node.js, AWS, Zapier, CRM/API integrations, and Stripe, but does not publicly identify the underlying voice/telephony providers, contracts, or portability terms (https://flippa.com/12206758-ai-voice-agent-saas-white-label-platform-1-000-users-40-countries-1-hr-day-owner-time-bootstrapped-recurring-revenue). A UK buyer acquiring a US-registered Stripe business may need a new UK Stripe account and a support-assisted data transfer; Stripe says an account’s country cannot be changed (https://support.stripe.com/questions/transferring-a-stripe-account-for-a-business-acquired-by-a-legal-entity-in-a-different-country). The product supports outbound sales calls, so compliance is material: UK ICO guidance requires specific consent for automated marketing calls (https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/direct-marketing-guidance/plan-direct-marketing/?q=consent), and the FCC treats AI-generated voices as artificial/prerecorded voices under the TCPA (https://docs.fcc.gov/public/attachments/FCC-24-17A1.pdf). No public evidence establishes jurisdiction-specific consent controls in the acquired product.
defensible_asset: Potential switching costs exist if customers have deployed customized workflows, CRM/API connections, and Zapier automations, all of which the listing describes (https://flippa.com/12206758-ai-voice-agent-saas-white-label-platform-1-000-users-40-countries-1-hr-day-owner-time-bootstrapped-recurring-revenue). However, no customer-level retention cohorts, migration costs, workflow export restrictions, or proof that integrations drive retention are public. No compiled proprietary dataset, maintained rules engine, or network effect is evidenced. Treat switching-cost moat as unproven pending customer and churn evidence.
build_effort: Moderate to high transition effort for a solo operator: buying an existing React/Node/AWS product avoids a greenfield build, but the public listing does not provide code, architecture, vendor-account, security, deployment, or support documentation (https://flippa.com/12206758-ai-voice-agent-saas-white-label-platform-1-000-users-40-countries-1-hr-day-owner-time-bootstrapped-recurring-revenue). Before relying on agents, a technical owner would need seller-assisted access transfer, reproducible deployment and recovery, telephony/provider cost reconciliation, and live-call and integration QA. The listing does not substantiate low-touch post-close operations.
channel: Use organic SEO, integration and app marketplaces, inbound marketplace listings, and opt-in technology/agency partnerships; the listing itself says its acquisition is primarily SEO and word of mouth (https://flippa.com/12206758-ai-voice-agent-saas-white-label-platform-1-000-users-40-countries-1-hr-day-owner-time-bootstrapped-recurring-revenue). Avoid unsolicited email, SMS, DMs, and calls. Keep customer acquisition separate from customers’ outbound-call use cases, which require consent and jurisdiction-specific controls; UK automated marketing calls need specific consent under ICO guidance (https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/direct-marketing-guidance/plan-direct-marketing/?q=consent).
owner_hours_per_week: unverified; the listing title says less than 1 hour per day but gives no time log or definition of a day, so it does not establish at most 5 hours per week (https://flippa.com/12206758-ai-voice-agent-saas-white-label-platform-1-000-users-40-countries-1-hr-day-owner-time-bootstrapped-recurring-revenue)
automation_reason: 55% is my estimate, not a measured property of this business. Agents could handle routine support triage, documentation, onboarding steps, billing follow-ups, reporting, and SEO drafts around the listed SaaS, Stripe, Zapier, and CRM workflows. Human time would remain for production incidents, voice-quality review, customer escalations, security and legal decisions, vendor management, and complex churn or sales conversations. The public listing supplies no task or staffing breakdown to validate the estimate (https://flippa.com/12206758-ai-voice-agent-saas-white-label-platform-1-000-users-40-countries-1-hr-day-owner-time-bootstrapped-recurring-revenue).
listing_check: Revenue: Flippa says revenue, primary expenses, and traffic were reviewed and Stripe/Google Analytics are connected, but the underlying evidence and period are hidden; Flippa itself advises buyers to request underlying financial evidence (https://flippa.com/12206758-ai-voice-agent-saas-white-label-platform-1-000-users-40-countries-1-hr-day-owner-time-bootstrapped-recurring-revenue). Churn: 9% overall is displayed, but its period, definition, and cohort basis are unverified. Owner time: less than 1 hour/day is a title claim only and does not prove <=5 hours/week. Price/profit: the public page now shows $525K and $7,282 monthly profit, or 6.0x annualized displayed profit; MRR of $4,297 does not reconcile with the displayed profit and 70% margin without a revenue bridge. The supplied $350K price conflicts with the reopened listing. Transferability: no public IP, customer-contract, source-code, or voice-provider transfer terms are shown. Stripe requires support-assisted ownership changes; if the buyer entity is UK-based and the Stripe account is US-based, Stripe says a new account and data-transfer request are needed (https://support.stripe.com/questions/transfer-a-stripe-account-to-a-different-entity-due-to-a-business-sale-or-acquisition?locale=en-GB; https://support.stripe.com/questions/transferring-a-stripe-account-for-a-business-acquired-by-a-legal-entity-in-a-different-country). Seller dependence: the listing says the founders are selling while shifting focus, but provides no handover scope, support commitment, or dependency analysis (https://flippa.com/12206758-ai-voice-agent-saas-white-label-platform-1-000-users-40-countries-1-hr-day-owner-time-bootstrapped-recurring-revenue).
moat_assessment: Conditional and not yet demonstrated. The advertised CRM/API/Zapier connections and customer workflow configurations could create switching costs, but 9% churn has no stated time basis and there is no public evidence that embedded workflows materially reduce cancellations (https://flippa.com/12206758-ai-voice-agent-saas-white-label-platform-1-000-users-40-countries-1-hr-day-owner-time-bootstrapped-recurring-revenue). Because the required moat must be evidenced, count this as a moat failure until customer-level retention and workflow-dependence evidence is supplied.
desk_test: Free one-day acquisition gate through the existing Flippa listing: request NDA/data-room access, then reconcile 12 months of Stripe transactions and bank deposits to monthly recurring revenue, usage fees, refunds, expenses, and the claimed $7,282 profit; obtain the definition and cohort calculation behind 9% churn, owner-time records, and read-only analytics. Ask for seller-assisted confirmation of code/IP, hosting, telephony-provider, and customer-contract transfer, plus Stripe’s cross-country transfer path. If the revenue bridge, transfer path, or owner-hours evidence is unavailable or inconsistent, make no offer.
red_flags: Do not treat this as a qualified acquisition yet: current public asking price is $525K rather than the supplied $350K; MRR, profit, and margin do not reconcile publicly; churn period and owner hours are unknown; Stripe may require a cross-country account/data migration; customer workflow switching costs are asserted but not proven; and recent launches show rapid competition. The listing also describes outbound sales functionality, which creates jurisdiction-specific consent and compliance exposure (Flippa: https://flippa.com/12206758-ai-voice-agent-saas-white-label-platform-1-000-users-40-countries-1-hr-day-owner-time-bootstrapped-recurring-revenue; Stripe: https://support.stripe.com/questions/transferring-a-stripe-account-for-a-business-acquired-by-a-legal-entity-in-a-different-country; ICO: https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/direct-marketing-guidance/plan-direct-marketing/?q=consent).
